title: Action Budgets, Iteration Caps, and Cost Governors

questions.question: An autonomous agent enters a repeated polling loop. Which type of limit can stop rapid spending before a monthly cap is reached?
options: A schema enum for the polling tool input
A weekly report that summarizes costs afterward
A model alias that hides the provider name
A financial velocity limit over a short time window
questions.explanation: A velocity limit measures spend over a short rolling window, so it can stop a rapid polling loop before monthly cost accumulates. A weekly report observes the bill after the burst rather than cutting it off.

questions.question: Which pair limits one completion's size and the total number of loop iterations?
options: velocity limit and monthly cap
prompt caching and context windowing
max_tokens and max_turns
max_budget_usd and allowed_tools
questions.explanation: `max_tokens` caps one completion; `max_turns` limits the number of loop iterations. A velocity limit and monthly cap constrain spend over time, not response size and iteration count.

questions.question: An agent has a per-task dollar cap, but it can call one expensive tool hundreds of times. Which layer addresses this risk most directly?
options: A context window
A read-only tracing span
A model alias
A per-tool call cap
questions.explanation: A per-tool cap limits repetition of one expensive action, such as hundreds of status polls, before the overall task budget fires. A model alias changes routing, not how many calls a tool can make.

questions.question: What does the lesson say happens when any configured budget cap fires?
options: Silently raise the cap to match the observed spend from the prior run
Keep the run active but switch to a longer context
Delete the cost history and retry from the beginning
Abort the session, record the cap, and use a separate re-enable path
questions.explanation: When a configured cap fires, abort the session, record the trigger, and require a separate re-enable action. Automatically raising the cap lets the same run bypass the control designed to stop it.

questions.question: A team has a monthly cap but sees a five-second retry loop burn money rapidly. Which missing control would catch it earlier?
options: A short-window velocity threshold
A per-month usage summary
A context compaction rule
A model alias for the primary route
questions.explanation: A five-second retry loop can exceed a short-window spend-rate threshold within minutes; a monthly cap may wait until substantial cost has accrued. A monthly report is too slow for rapid runaway spending.

questions.question: An expensive download is legitimate in some runs but can unexpectedly consume a large budget. What control adds a human decision at the right point?
options: A daily report after the download finishes
A larger iteration cap for all sessions
A HITL checkpoint before the expensive action
A cache of the agent's system prompt
questions.explanation: A human checkpoint before the expensive download decides whether its cost is justified before it is incurred. A report afterward records spending but cannot prevent the charge already made.
